I am 38 years old, finished primary school, and have only been farming on my own for three years. Before that I worked outside, but now I am back home in Quzhou County. My family has five people to feed, so I cannot afford big losses. I learn mainly by watching my neighbors and asking the seed shop what varieties sell well.

I have 16.1 mu of land and a well for irrigation. My cropping system is built around eggplant because that is what the vegetable buyers in our area want most, and the price is usually good. But I keep 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the foundation — it gives me grain for my family and some steady income. The other 9.1 mu I use for vegetables: 5 mu for eggplant, 2.1 mu for autumn cabbage, and 2 mu for spring cauliflower.

Right now it is early spring. My winter wheat on 7 mu is greening up. I sowed it last October with an improved local variety. I will go through the field lightly with the rotary tiller to break the crust, then topdress with urea when the wheat starts jointing. I will irrigate three times from my well: once now for green-return, once at heading, and once during grain filling. For pests, I spray herbicide early and maybe two more times for aphids and rust, so four times total. I hope to get around 500 kg per mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize on the same 7 mu. I use no-tillage direct seeding right into the wheat stubble — everyone here does that now to save time and keep moisture. The maize needs two irrigations if the summer rains are weak, and I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for borers. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

Eggplant is my main cash crop on 5 mu. I buy hybrid seedlings from the market because my own seedlings always get damping-off. I rotary-till deep, spread manure and compound fertilizer as base, then transplant in May. Eggplant needs water every week in the dry season, so I irrigate about 10 times from the well. I topdress with urea and potassium fertilizer twice during fruiting. Pests are bad — aphids, mites, wilt — so I spray about 8 times. If the weather cooperates I can get 3,500 kg per mu.

For cauliflower, I plant 2 mu in spring with hybrid seeds. It needs steady moisture, so I irrigate 6 times and spray 5 times for caterpillars and downy mildew. I expect about 4,000 kg per mu.

My 2.1 mu of cabbage I plant in late summer for autumn harvest. Cabbage stores well and I can sell it through the winter. I rotary-till, apply base fertilizer, and topdress twice. I irrigate 6 times and spray 6 times for pests. I hope for 3,000 kg per mu.

My fertilizer use is simple: compound fertilizer as base, then urea for topdressing, and extra potassium for eggplant. I do not calculate exact pure nutrients — I go by bags and by watching the crop color. But roughly, I put more on the vegetables than on the cereals because vegetables take more out of the soil.
